title: Virtual reality in palliative care - improving quality of life through immersive personalised technology
summary: Palliative patients often suffer from chronic pain, emotional stress, anxiety and social isolation. Virtual reality (VR) can help to increase subjective well-being through distraction and positive sensory impressions. With the aim of establishing a ‘proof of principle’, this study will investigate the hypothesis of whether personalised, intermittent immersions in soothing virtual realities (VR) can have positive effects on the condition of palliative care patients in the sense of an ‘accompanying therapy’ and whether the effects on patients in palliative care units differ from those in hospices or outpatient palliative care. The VR application is to be investigated in 150 palliative care patients. The aim is to investigate the effectiveness of VR as an immersive therapy to improve well-being, pain, depression, anxiety and blood pressure.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient receiving palliative care
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 years
- Refusal to participate in the study
- Lack of capacity to consent
- Known manifest epilepsy
- Infectious diseases (3MRGN, 4MRGN, MRSA, etc.)
- Mental impairments that prevent understanding of the questionnaire or the study or consent:
1. diagnosed mental illnesses (e.g. severe depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, severe anxiety disorders) 
2. cognitive impairments (e.g. dementia, intellectual impairments, cognitive disorders due to a neurological disease)
3. acute mental crises (e.g. suicidal thoughts or acute psychotic episodes)
4. cognitive and language impairments (e.g. severe language disorders, aphasic disorders)
